newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 18.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Wednesday:
* Lucent Technologies Inc and Philips Electronics NV have agreed to merge their consumer communications products businesses into a jointly owned company.
* Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd has agreed to acquire Celebrity Cruise LInes Inc for about $1.3 billion in cash, stock and assumed debt, giving rival Carnival Cruises a run for its money.
* The House Banking Committee voted to allow bank holding companies to acquire nonfinancial businesses as long as they made up no more than 15 percent of the banking company's gross domestic revenue.
* Barney's Inc, the famed clothier, is closing its original store in Manhattan along with other underperforming stores in Houston, Dallas, and Troy, Mich.
* Motorola Inc plans to build a $12.9 billion satellite network to provide telecommunications services around the world.
* AMR Corp's American Eagle has ordered 67 aircraft from Bombardier of Canada and Embraer of Brazil worth about $1.4 billion.

* Market Place: Tele-Communications Inc is in a deal to buy back a block of stock owned by the estate of TCI's late founder, Bob Magness, dodging the possibility of the estate selling the shares on the open market.
* The Dow Jones Industrials dipped by 11.31 points, closing at 7760.78.
* Senate Republicans have proposed a offered up a package of tax cuts that the Clinton administration said slightly improves upon the House Republican version that was passed last week.
* NBC executive John Agoglia, who headed negotiations on a variety of deals for the network, is stepping down.
* A leading observer of ad spending predicts that marketers will spend a record $186 billion this year in the United States.
* Tobacco settlement talks hit an impasses as negotiators continue to haggle over the issues of punitive damages and federal nicotine regulations.
* Microsoft Corp is spending $80 million to create a research lab at Cambridge University, one of the world's best known centers of learning.

* U.S. Rep. Dick Armey, the House majority leader, plans to introduce legislation to reduce the cost of auto insurance by giving motorists the option to drop coverage for pain and suffering caused in an accident.

* Certain economic indicators suggest America is entering a similar golden era as that experienced from 1946 to 1973. But, in fact, people are working harder to maintain their standard of living and incomes have stagnated.
* The Consumer Price Index rose one-tenth of 1 percent in May.
